task_brief: Day 2 of "Data and Visualization" (unit 4, grade 7) is a worked-model trace on spreadsheets and formulas. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Analyze an approved dataset and publish an honest visualization with limits. Today's work contributes to that by handling spreadsheets and formulas at the explicit model stage, against the unit's wider topics of data collection ethics, spreadsheets and formulas, cleaning data, and charts. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Work through the complete central input printed in activity_setup for spreadsheets and formulas, one step at a time rather than reading it straight through. For each step, write what changed and why that step is legal. Build a trace table with one row per step showing the values or states before and after. Then change exactly one line, value, or condition in the model, predict the new result before running or re-tracing it, and record whether your prediction was right. Explain in your own words the rule that makes spreadsheets and formulas behave the way the model shows. The activity_setup block below supplies the complete central input, exact specification, execution method, test cases, debugging target, and equal-credit manual simulation; use those exact materials rather than waiting for another handout, account, service, or tool. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about spreadsheets and formulas, and it belongs to "Data and Visualization", which also covers separate topics such as data collection ethics. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about spreadsheets and formulas; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.

central_input.title: Inline spreadsheets and formulas code case
central_input.purpose: Use this exact fictional case to investigate spreadsheets and formulas; no other file, model, dataset, or account is needed.

expected_behavior_and_specification: The procedure must execute every supplied step in order; the main input must return open > check > save.
An empty step list must return an empty string, and a one-step list must retain that step.
The submitted explanation must connect the observed control flow or data state to spreadsheets and formulas, not merely state the final number.
The smallest test case must be tried and its actual result compared with the expected result.

execution_method.primary: No-install browser method: open any browser developer console, paste the complete starter code, press Enter, and record the output or exact error text.
execution_method.local_optional: If Node.js is already installed, save the unchanged snippet as activity.js and run `node activity.js`; installing Node.js is not required.
execution_method.no_computer_required: The hand-trace route below is a complete execution method and earns identical credit.

debugging_target.observed_failure: Iteration begins at index 1, so the first instruction is silently skipped and the main input returns check > save.
debugging_target.target: Repair the initial index, explain the sequence invariant, and rerun all three tests.
debugging_target.passing_change: Iteration begins at index 0; all three tests retain every step in order.
debugging_target.scope_note: Diagnosing the state, control-flow, or data defect and connecting the repair to spreadsheets and formulas is the central evidence.

equal_credit_alternative.method: Paper or notes-app simulation; this earns exactly the same score as running code.
steps: Make one row for each statement or loop check and copy the starting input exactly.
Record every variable, object field, selected item, and output after that step.
Circle the first row where the actual state stops matching the specification.
Apply the one repair named in your explanation and trace all three tests again.
equal_credit_alternative.evidence_to_submit: The completed trace, the one-line corrected condition, and an expected-versus-actual table for all three tests.

test_or_check_criteria: The trace table has one row per step and shows values or states both before and after that step.
Every step carries a written reason that step is legal, not just a restatement of what happened.
Exactly one deliberate change was made to the model, with a prediction recorded before the re-run and the outcome after.
The rule governing spreadsheets and formulas is restated in the student's own words rather than copied from the model.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Provide a screen-reader-compatible editor, adjustable font size and contrast, and a complete keyboard-only workflow. An offline paper-and-trace route is available for every task here and is scored identically to an on-screen one.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never require a real password, private message, precise location, account credential, or identifiable image.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify, not as an authority or a substitute for learner work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting spreadsheets and formulas.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for spreadsheets and formulas follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for spreadsheets and formulas, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for spreadsheets and formulas works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of spreadsheets and formulas, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking spreadsheets and formulas mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply spreadsheets and formulas under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on spreadsheets and formulas rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
